canonical_statement: The study evaluated how renal impairment affects cefazolin persistence in serum and urinary concentrations, with comparative observations on cephalothin, protein binding, and hemodialysis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This study was designed to determine the effect of renal impairment on the persistence of this drug in serum.

canonical_statement: The study included six healthy volunteers and 11 patients with varying degrees of renal impairment; two renal patients were receiving chronic intermittent hemodialysis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Six healthy volunteers and 11 patients with various degrees of renal impairment were included in this study.

population.label: Healthy volunteers and patients with renal impairment

canonical_statement: All six healthy volunteers and four uremic patients received a single 500 mg intramuscular cefazolin dose.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All normal subjects and four uremic patients were given single im injections of 500 mg of both cefazolin and cephalothin.

population.label: Healthy volunteers plus four uremic patients

canonical_statement: The same six healthy volunteers and four uremic patients received a single 500 mg intramuscular cephalothin dose at least one week apart from cefazolin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All normal subjects and four uremic patients were given single im injections of 500 mg of both cefazolin and cephalothin.

population.label: Healthy volunteers plus four uremic patients

canonical_statement: Blood was sampled through 12 hours after dosing, with additional 24-, 36-, and 48-hour samples in patients with significant renal impairment; urine was collected through 48 hours.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: additional samples were drawn at 24, 36, and 48 hr after injection. Urine was collected

canonical_statement: Six normal subjects received cefazolin 500 mg intramuscularly every 8 hours for four days; two renal patients received a 500 mg loading dose followed by 250 mg every 12 or 24 hours.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Normal volunteers were given 500 mg im every 8 hr. The two uremic patients received 500 mg as a loading dose.

canonical_statement: Serum and urine cefazolin and cephalothin concentrations were measured by a cup-plate microbiologic assay using Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 6538P.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cefazolin and cephalothin in serum and urine were assayed by the cup-plate method.

canonical_statement: Serum protein binding was measured by equilibrium dialysis, and the measured binding percentages were used to estimate free-drug concentrations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: tested for the degree of binding to proteins by the equilibrium-dialysis method previously described.

canonical_statement: Creatinine clearance was measured from serum and urine creatinine; half-life was derived from semilog concentration decline, and apparent volume of distribution used a one-compartment open model.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The volume of distribution was obtained from curve fitting of data to the pharmacokinetic one-compartment, open-model.

canonical_statement: After equal 500 mg intramuscular doses in normal volunteers, total serum cefazolin concentrations were reported as four- to sixfold higher than cephalothin concentrations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: peak levels of total cefazolin in blood were four to six times greater than those of cephalothin.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: fold difference in total serum concentration

canonical_statement: After equal doses in normal volunteers, free serum cefazolin concentrations were approximately threefold higher than free cephalothin concentrations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: concentrations of free drug were only three times higher.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: fold difference in free serum concentration

canonical_statement: In normal subjects after a single intramuscular dose, mean serum half-life was 1.91 ± 0.23 hours for cefazolin and 0.58 ± 0.11 hours for cephalothin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 1.91 ± 0.23 hr and 0.58 ± 0.11 hr, respectively.

canonical_statement: Cefazolin serum half-life increased as renal function declined, with a marked rise when creatinine clearance fell below 20 mL/min.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A precipitous rise in duration of half-life was observed when the creatinine clearance fell below 20 ml/min.

population.label: Participants spanning normal to impaired renal function

canonical_statement: The relationship between cefazolin overall elimination rate and creatinine clearance was linear, with regression y = 0.02 + 0.003x and r = 0.984.

population.label: Participants spanning normal to impaired renal function

canonical_statement: In one hemodialysis patient, cefazolin serum half-life decreased from 45.8 hours between dialysis sessions to 27.8 hours during dialysis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The half-life in serum was reduced from 45.8 and 32.0 hr to 27.8 and 20.5 hr, respectively.

canonical_statement: In the second hemodialysis patient, cefazolin serum half-life decreased from 32.0 hours between dialysis sessions to 20.5 hours during dialysis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The half-life in serum was reduced from 45.8 and 32.0 hr to 27.8 and 20.5 hr, respectively.

canonical_statement: In normal subjects, mean serum protein binding was 83.9% ± 1.4% for cefazolin and 65.2% ± 4.3% for cephalothin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 83.9% ± 1.4% and 65.2% ± 4.3%, respectively.

canonical_statement: Across patients with renal impairment, cefazolin protein binding ranged from 61.6% to 84.7%.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the protein binding of cefazolin varied from 84.7% to 61.6%.

canonical_statement: Table 1 reported normal-subject cefazolin protein binding 83.9% ± 1.4%, apparent volume of distribution 12.2% ± 3.4% of body weight, and peak serum concentration 42.9 ± 7.3 µg/mL.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: mean apparent volume of distribution as percent body weight

canonical_statement: Table 1 renal group 2 had cefazolin protein binding 74.8% ± 2.4%, apparent volume of distribution 14.1% ± 4.5% of body weight, and peak serum concentration 65.5 ± 11.7 µg/mL.
Table 1 renal group 3 had cefazolin protein binding 63.4% ± 1.5% and apparent volume of distribution 23.0% ± 4.3% of body weight; both differed significantly from normal subjects.

quantitative_result.effect_measure: mean apparent volume of distribution as percent body weight

canonical_statement: Normal volunteers had an average cefazolin urinary recovery of 74.2% by 12 hours after a single intramuscular dose.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In normal volunteers recovery was virtually complete in 12 hr (average recovery, 74.2%).

quantitative_result.effect_measure: mean percent dose recovered in urine

canonical_statement: Patients with creatinine clearance ≤15 mL/min had peak urinary cefazolin concentrations ranging from 175 to 400 µg/mL despite reduced urinary excretion.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: patients with creatinine clearances ≤ 15 ml/min had peak urinary concentrations of cefazolin that ranged from 175 µg/ml to 400 µg/ml.

population.label: Renal impairment with creatinine clearance ≤15 mL/min

quantitative_result.effect_measure: peak urinary concentration range lower bound

canonical_statement: Eight-hour urinary recovery of cefazolin increased with creatinine clearance; Figure 6 reported y = 2.33x^0.73 and r = 0.926.

population.label: Participants spanning normal to impaired renal function

canonical_statement: During four days of cefazolin 500 mg every 8 hours in normal subjects, mean peak serum concentration was 52.8 µg/mL and remained similar across treatment days.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Peak concentrations of cefazolin in serum of normal subjects receiving 500 mg every 8 hr averaged 52.8 µg/ml.

canonical_statement: In the normal-subject multiple-dose study, average maximal and minimal urinary cefazolin concentrations were 2,200 and 400 µg/mL, respectively.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The average maximal and minimal urinary concentrations achieved during the study period were 2,200 and 400 µg/ml, respectively.

canonical_statement: Two uremic patients given a 500 mg cefazolin loading dose followed by 250 mg at approximately one half-life intervals maintained serum concentrations of 36.9–78.0 µg/mL without significant accumulation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: adequate concentrations in serum (36.9–78.0 µg/ml), with no significant accumulation over the four-day period.

canonical_statement: In the two uremic multiple-dose patients, urinary cefazolin concentrations remained above 100 µg/mL.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Urinary concentrations in these two patients were consistently > 100 µg/ml.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that cefazolin offered higher and more prolonged free-drug concentrations than cephalothin while having similar antimicrobial activity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cefazolin appears to be a promising addition to the cephalosporin family in that it provides higher and more prolonged levels of free drug.

canonical_statement: For normal renal function, the authors extrapolated that either half the cephalothin dose or twice the customary cephalothin dosing interval might provide at least equivalent exposure.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: either half the dose or administration at twice the customary interval established for cephalothin should be at least equivalent.

canonical_statement: For renal impairment, the authors preferred a loading dose followed by one-half the dose each drug half-life for relatively safe beta-lactams because of simplicity and sustained serum levels.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We prefer to use method no. 1 with relatively safe agents such as the penicillins and cephalosporins.

canonical_statement: Only two patients were studied during and between hemodialysis, limiting inference about dialytic cefazolin removal.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Only two patients were studied both during and between hemodialysis.

canonical_statement: The authors stated that optimal dosing in normal renal function still required clinical trials and that cefazolin’s final role depended on demonstrating lack of major toxicity and relative cost.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This will have to be determined in clinical trials.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This work was supported in part by the Veterans Administration and by a grant from Smith, Kline & French Laboratories.
